page: Amazon Web Services m8id.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz across 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration includes 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution. In addition, the instance integrates 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and offers an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

The underlying Intel processor incorporates hardware extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), and hardware cryptography accelerators. Benchmark tests reveal competitive single-threaded capabilities, registering strong results in single-threaded gzip compression at 34.13 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.41 GB/sec, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 2204.0. Text processing performance and small model LLM text generation (350.53 tokens/sec) rank in the top tier, whereas multi-core compute tests such as stress-ng (17293.19) and PassMark CPU (29279.13) register in the middle tier.

The inclusion of a 950 GB NVMe SSD volume directly on the host provides high-speed scratch space and transient data handling without relying strictly on external block storage, improving efficiency for disk-intensive workflows. However, workloads requiring persistent retention across stopping cycles must account for instance store ephemerality. With balanced memory and compute resources, the m8id.4xlarge is well aligned for relational database hosting, Redis in-memory caches, CI/CD compilation jobs, and general enterprise backend services.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.4xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by a 16-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, paired with 64 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz and 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Built on the AWS Nitro system, it delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and incorporates advanced hardware extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks highlight solid single-thread performance, with strong results in gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and text processing, alongside average multi-core compute throughput. The integrated local NVMe SSD delivers low-latency scratch storage, though data on the volume is ephemeral. This combination of dedicated x86_64 compute, fast memory, and bundled local storage makes the m8id.4xlarge well suited for backend web serving, transactional database workloads, Redis caching, and CI/CD pipelines.
